questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Please explain: *
Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Crucial in choosing this study destination was the opportunities to learn the french language as well as the opportunity to gain a deeper understanding of french cultural. I was also very drawn by the idea of learning within the prestigous and well respected academics facilities of the sorbonne

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: How easy it was to find relevant information was very depending on what it was concerning. Copenhagen university were good at displayed the information in an accessible manner. It was very varying how easy it was to gain relevant information from Sorbonne University.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I was invited to a introduction meeting for exchange studies.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
What should future exchange students know about on campus housing? *
How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I lived at the Mexican House in Cité Universitaire. It was relatively easy to find this. I would absolutely recommend others to apply for this housing.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Well I would say that I happy that I didnt live off campus in the form of an appartment, as I have heard that to be filled with uncertainties. I would say that their a certain security that comes with living in a dormitory, which is very called for, when one moves to a big city like Paris.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer:
Have my university had given me the nomination, I had to send a formel application to my host university: my application consisted of  a recommendation from a teacher, a letter of motivation, my grades and a b2 language test. I also had to write what subjects I was interested in taking. 
What follows were many differents bureaucratic processes: the learning agreement for example

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The help consisted in mails from Outgoing Exchange and Sorbonne varying in accessibility. One could write to the head secratary for exchange. She was usually very helpful

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Once I was at the institution, was where the actual registration began.  I got all the classes I wanted

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: My main advice would be "Be patient". You WILL get registrate, even if the process is chaotic and long, as it is of the interest of the university that you do. My second advice would be to talk to people who have already as well as people who are going and are in the same situation as you.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I took courses in English as well as courses in English. I found the academic level of the courses in French to match the level at home. I found the academic level of the courses in English to be general a bit (som times quite a bit) lower, that what I was used to.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The style of teaching was very distinctly different from what I was used. It was a teaching approach, which was less open and dialogical that the general teaching approach at UCPH.  The teaching approach, one could say, is more one-sided  and very much based on a proces of the teaching saying stuff and the students writing exactly what they are saying down.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
I took the following courses:
1.  Méthod de la civilisation
2. Société britannique
3. Arts et Médias
4. Cultures sérielles
5.  Perfectionnement expression orale en tandem anglais-français
6. Art français
7.  Cinéma et philosophie
8.  Langue française - avancé B2
9.  Le melodrame
10. Les cinémas anticoloniaux et postcoloniaux

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your second semester. *
What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
I would warmly recommend future exchange to take the courses specifically intended the exchange students. Mine were the following:
 Art français
Cinéma et philosophie
Langue française - avancé B2

questions.answer: I found the general cost of living to me very expensive.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There were various activities offered by the host institution. Unfortunately, I was not good at seeking them and therefore I dont know what was offered.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: As I didnt myself go to these activities, I unfortunately do not have a lot to recommend in this regard.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: I would absolutely recommend students to go to some of the small towns outside of Paris: The town of Monet's house and the town of Van Gogh. Going to the cinema is surpringly cheap in Paris, so I would recommend that as well.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: I found it to be rather difficult. However it helpful a lot, that there were many in the same situation

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: I would recommend to seek various WhatsApp groups made for exchange students to connect.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I did not fin the cultural differences particularly challenging - the differences were mostly just fascinating

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I found the big "flaneur culture" and the cultural of going to meseums and to the cinema to be a very fun cultural praxis to embrace and engage in.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
I was say the following:
1. Make sure to taake as many of the subject specially made for exchange students as possible
2. In order to make the work load slightly more barrable, I would recommend taking courses in English
3. As the workload is so high (10 courses which means 10 midterm exams, 10 final exams and several presentations and papers to be made) one very quickly how to take on a very light attitude towards academic performance, as the workload makes very hard to do perfectly in every subject (especially if you want to explore the city).

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Embrace French Cafe Culture!

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The most rewarding part of bettering my french and my knowledge of French culture, through the courses in French I took.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The greatest challenge differently was the big workload (10 courses which means 10 midterm exams, 10 final exams and several presentations and papers to be made). Back home we usually only take 2 courses.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
